messages.author: de2c0368d9349f5a
messages.subject: DIF Test
parts:
Hi all,

I have a total of 72 items and three groups, each one answering a specific test ), such that:

Items 1-22: presented only to group 1
Items 23-30: presented to groups 1 and 2
Items 31-42: presented only to group 2
Items 43-52: presented to groups 2 and 3
Items 53-72: presented only to group 3


I am doing a multiple groups analysis with the following codes:

model.prior <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-72
                         CONSTRAINB = (23-30,43-52,a1),
                          (23-30,43-52,d),
                          (23-30,43-52,g)
                          PRIOR = (1-72, a1, lnorm, 1,1),
                          (1-72, d, norm, 0, 3),
                          (1-72, g, norm, -1.1,1.1)')
resultML3P<-multipleGroup(mYmirt, model=model.prior ,
                          group = vgrupo,itemtype='3PL',
              SE=TRUE,method='EM',TOL=0.0001,quadpts=40,
              invariance=c('free_means',
                           'free_var','slopes','intercepts'))

where "mYirt" is the binary matrix (with NA, since not all subjects answer all items). I've got the following issues concernig DIF analysis:
 
DIF(resultML3P, c('a1', 'd'),items2test=c(23:30,43:52),Wald = TRUE,p.adjust = 'fdr')
Error in solve.default(L %*% covB %*% t(L)) : 
  Lapack routine dgesv: system is exactly singular: U[1,1] = 0

and

DIF(resultML3P, c('a1', 'd'),items2test=c(23:30,43:52)) did not run.

I think that this due to fact that DIF(.) tries to perform the analysis with all three groups but only two of them answer the above items (c(23:30,43:52)). Is there any way for handling that?

Best,

Caio

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF Test
parts:
This is likely a problem of generality, which is where wrapper functions like DIF() are going to have a harder time working around data limitations without some strong checks. I think the checks are possible though, in that I could at least check that some data exists across the groups for the respective items in order to potentially perform a valid estimation of these models. A reproducible example would be helpful to save me some time trying to recreate the problem on my end. Thanks.

Phil
